quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Your motorcycle starts to weave while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Grip the handlebars tighter and speed up to get past the hazard.
Ride in a zigzag pattern.
Move to the shoulder to avoid the grooves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is usually not dangerous. Stay relaxed and ride straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging to compensate is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: A dog is chasing you. What should you do?

options.text: Kick the dog away.
Stop and wait for it to lose interest.
Swerve around the dog.
Slow down to approach it, then speed up suddenly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to approach it, then speed up suddenly.
questions.explanation: Dogs are often attracted to motorcycles. Downshift and approach the dog slowly. Then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.question: At night, how should your following distance compare to daytime riding?

options.text: You should stay farther back from the vehicle ahead at night.
You should stay closer to the vehicle ahead at night.
You should maintain the same distance day and night.
Following distance does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should stay farther back from the vehicle ahead at night.
questions.explanation: At night, it is hard to judge distances because shadows and light are missing or unclear. Stay farther back from the vehicle ahead at night than you would during the day.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, use both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: When riding downhill on a motorcycle with a sidecar, how does stopping compare to a motorcycle without a sidecar?

options.text: Stopping will be easier with a sidecar.
Stopping will take longer with a sidecar.
You cannot stop with a sidecar.
Stopping is about the same with or without a sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping will take longer with a sidecar.
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight to your motorcycle, which requires more braking power. Downhill riding also makes stopping take longer. Together, these factors mean stopping takes much longer with a sidecar.

questions.question: What happens if you shift to a lower gear while going too fast?

options.text: The motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
The horn may sound.
The motorcycle may jerk and the front tire may skid.
The motorcycle may jerk and a warning light will turn on.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift to a lower gear while going too fast, the motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid, causing you to lose control. Always slow down enough before shifting to a lower gear.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake control usually located?

options.text: On the right handlebar.
On the left handlebar.
Near the left foot.
Near the right foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right foot.
questions.explanation: The rear brake is normally operated with your right foot.

questions.question: When slowing down or stopping, what should you do with the gears?

options.text: Shift up through the gears.
Shift down through the gears.
Take the motorcycle out of gear.
Stay in the same gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down through the gears.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: Near the front so experienced riders can watch them.
They will get lost if they lead the group.
At the front because they may slow the group down elsewhere.
Anywhere except the front because they ride too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the front so experienced riders can watch them.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can easily watch and monitor them.

questions.question: Why is a flat front tire especially dangerous?

options.text: It affects your steering.
The front tire provides power, so you lose acceleration.
The flat tire shakes the bike, making mirrors hard to use.
You won't be able to use the brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It affects your steering.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is very dangerous because it makes steering difficult. If your front tire goes flat while riding, safely exit the road as quickly as possible.

questions.question: Your lane position should help you:

options.text: Show other drivers what you plan to do.
Stop other drivers from passing you.
Get to your destination as fast as possible.
Stay in the blind spots of other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Good lane position protects your lane and tells other drivers what you plan to do next.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Is the best way to know they see you.
Is not worth the effort.
Does not mean they will give you the right of way.
Guarantees they will give you the right of way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they will give you the right of way.
questions.explanation: Never count on eye contact as proof that a driver will give you the right of way. Drivers often look directly at a motorcycle rider but do not see them.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest
On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: A face shield:

options.text: Protects your eyes and face.
Is not recommended.
Is required.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects your eyes and face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, impact-resistant face shield gives the most protection for your eyes and face. Glasses or sunglasses are not enough. In Vermont, you do not have to wear eye or face protection if your motorcycle has a windshield, but it is still recommended.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks that cross your lane at an angle, it is usually:

options.text: Safest to ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
Dangerous to ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
Not safe to cross tracks on a motorcycle.
Safest to cross the tracks by riding on the road shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safest to ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: When railroad tracks cross your lane at an angle, ride straight across them in your lane. Turning to cross at a 90-degree angle is dangerous because you might move into another lane of traffic.

questions.question: If your motorcycle begins to wobble, you should:

options.text: Speed up to stop the wobble.
Use the brakes slowly.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
Shift to a lower gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up—this makes the wobble worse. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly without fighting the wobble. Slowly close the throttle to slow down. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can.

questions.question: The front brake supplies how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?

options.text: About one-quarter
About one-half
About three-quarters
All of the stopping power

questions.correctAnswerText: About three-quarters
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: To protect a motorcycle rider, pants should:

options.text: Be made of soft material.
Be made of heavy material.
Fit loosely so they flap in the wind.
Be short and expose some leg.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be made of heavy material.
questions.explanation: Wear pants made of leather or sturdy synthetic material that cover your entire legs. Your clothing should fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind, but not so tight that it limits your movement.

questions.question: When changing lanes, riders should:

options.text: Only use their mirrors to check for other vehicles.
Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
Not worry about other traffic.
Brake hard to let any vehicles in their blind spot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should:

options.text: Only take a few minutes.
Take more than an hour.
Be complicated to do.
Not be done before every ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only take a few minutes.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. A thorough inspection usually takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: If you must ride over an obstacle, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Speed up, if possible.
Stay on your seat and remove your feet from the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as much as possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down. Approach it at a 90-degree angle if possible. Keep your motorcycle straight. Just before hitting it, ease off the throttle slightly to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Avoid sudden moves.
Use both brakes.
Brake quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake quickly.
questions.explanation: To ride safely on a slippery surface, slow down, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes gently if you need to stop.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle, how should they do it?

options.text: In a staggered formation.
In a pyramid formation.
One at a time.
In a splintered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, riders should pass one at a time. The second rider waits until the first rider is safely back in the original lane before passing. This pattern continues until all riders have passed.

questions.question: How can a motorcyclist stop other vehicles from sharing their lane?

options.text: Ride in the left portion of a lane.
Ride in the center portion of a lane.
Give dirty looks if another driver moves into their lane.
Ride in a zigzag pattern to fill up a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of a lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane. This makes it harder for other drivers to squeeze in next to you.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Use the front brake only.
Use the front brake first.
Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both the front and rear brakes at the same time.
